answer: A streaming DeepWalk variant replaces the usual batch pipeline (build the full graph, generate all random walks, then train skip-gram once) with an incremental one. As edges or nodes arrive, it generates random walks from the portion of the graph observed so far, and it updates the skip-gram embeddings online with stochastic gradient steps on those walks, so the model learns while the graph is still growing and does not need to store or revisit the whole graph. One tradeoff is accuracy versus timeliness: early embeddings are built from an incomplete and biased view of the graph (for example, nodes with few observed neighbors get poorly estimated vectors), and the embeddings can drift as new data arrives. Keeping them consistent or stable usually requires extra mechanisms such as periodic retraining, replaying old walks, or regularization, which add cost and complexity.
